items.title: MIT and Motional's CW-Net explains why self-driving cars make certain decisions
items.summary_en: MIT CSAIL researchers, working with autonomous-vehicle company Motional, built CW-Net (Concept-Wrapper Network), a system that translates an AV planner's internal reasoning into human-readable concepts such as 'approaching stopped vehicle' or 'close to cyclist' without changing the vehicle's driving performance. In closed-track and public-road tests around Las Vegas, CW-Net's explanations helped safety drivers and non-expert users predict vehicle behavior more accurately, and in one case exposed that a test planner was hallucinating a phantom stopped vehicle near a traffic cone, a pattern traced to its training data.
items.notes: Industry collaboration with Motional (Aptiv/Hyundai autonomous-vehicle venture); MIT News institutional article, independently cross-posted by MIT AeroAstro and MIT Schwarzman College of Computing with matching details. No separate arXiv preprint identified from available sources; direct access to news.mit.edu and csail.mit.edu was blocked in this collection environment, so this summary is built from search-engine-retrieved excerpts of the primary article plus corroborating mirrors, not a direct fetch.

items.title: MIT-led team publishes single-cell atlas of the brain's striatum linked to Huntington's, schizophrenia, and addiction
items.summary_en: A team led by Myriam Heiman (MIT Picower Institute), Manolis Kellis (MIT CSAIL professor of computer science), and Dana Gabuzda (Dana-Farber Cancer Institute) used single-cell RNA sequencing to catalog 31 neuron subpopulations in the brain's striatum, including two 'outlier' medium spiny neuron types implicated in schizophrenia, substance-use disorder, and depression. The study also identifies factors that may make specific striatal neurons more vulnerable to Huntington's disease, which the authors say could inform future drug development.
items.notes: This is primarily a computational-neuroscience/genomics study; the only CSAIL tie is co-senior-author Manolis Kellis. Tangential to core AI/ML research and possibly out of scope for an AI-frontier report — flagging for the Orchestrator to confirm inclusion or reassignment. Journal name and peer-review status could not be confirmed because direct access to news.mit.edu and eurekalert.org (which held the press release) was blocked in this collection environment; content is derived from search-engine excerpts of those primary sources.
